title: Rust's conjecture on the Tribonacci combinatorial-game sequences
statement:
Let $(X(n))_{n\geq 0}$ and $(Y(n))_{n\geq 0}$ be the sequences defined by the recursive combinatorial-game construction in the source. **Rust's conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$,

$$
X(Y(n))+Y(X(n))=2X(n)+2Y(n)-1.
$$

The conjecture was made by Dan Rust in 2022. The supplied text refutes it and states that there are infinitely many counterexamples, including $n=20$.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03996

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2022). “This shows that there are infinitely many counterexamples to Rust's conjecture, and one of them is $n = 20$.”
